tasks.short: Assess material availability and recommend responses to supply risks.

steps.what: Gather stock, demand, open orders and delivery performance.
Read market reports and supplier notices for availability risks.

loop.input: Approved market reports and supplier notices, with dates and source identifiers.
loop.output: Material, region, disruption, expected duration and supporting passages.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate dates and material identifiers; flag conflicting or missing information.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields go to the purchasing manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports describe disruptions in varied prose that fixed field mappings cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Compare coverage, lead times and alternative supply scenarios.
Validate uncertain delivery promises and operational constraints with suppliers and planners.
Write a recommendation on sourcing, stock and delivery priorities.

loop.input: Validated assumptions, calculated scenarios and the manager's preferred response.
loop.output: Availability brief with options, tradeoffs, uncertainties and source references.
loop.check: Match every figure to scenario outputs; the purchasing manager checks reasoning before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; unsupported recommendations are removed or written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: The explanation must connect changing supply evidence with operational tradeoffs.

steps.what: Agree material responses and approve changes requiring additional budget or operational tradeoffs.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {OPS_SYSTEM} records into a {BI} availability dashboard with deterministic scenarios. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare cited risk notes and briefs in {DOCS}; people validate uncertain promises and approve supply responses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material identifiers, delivery histories and forecasts were split across systems. Market signals required manual reading, and scenario work was often rebuilt for each review.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and planning functions can supply the core data. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building connectors and scenario calculations; bounded models can extract cited signals from prose.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier promises can be unreliable. Substitution constraints, demand changes and correlated disruptions still require commercial and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which supplier assurances deserve trust and balance continuity, cash, quality and customer commitments.

ambition.what: Weekly alternate-source activation decisions for critical materials

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting figures and more time testing assumptions with suppliers and planners. Existing approval limits remain; faster evidence supports more frequent alternate-source decisions.

reach.task: Assess alternate suppliers for threatened materials.
reach.learn: Learn qualification lead times, minimum orders and when a quotation represents usable capacity.

reach.task: Choose assortment substitutions when availability changes.
reach.learn: Learn demand substitution, margin effects and customer acceptance.

evidence.claim: Deterministic coverage calculations and scenario dashboards can automate much of the data preparation.
Slim4 forecasts demand and sets stock by item and store, supporting the planning component.
The Lasaulec vendor case reports stock down over 20% and availability above 98%; the period is unstated.

assumptions: The company has material-level order, receipt and stock records, with some spreadsheet scenario work.
Time shares describe the whole task across participating roles, not only the manager's keyboard time.
Judgement remains substantial, consistent with the supplied priors; collection and calculation are the main automation targets.
The first version covers one material category and uses existing access controls.
EU GDPR applies to personal data. Employee monitoring is excluded; consultation under national rules is included if the implementation affects working practices.
unknowns: Whether material identifiers match across the customer's systems.
Which data interfaces, market-report licences and supplier-use permissions are available.
Which materials are critical and what stock or sourcing changes require approval.
Which national rules and employee consultation procedures apply.
research_questions: Which shortage indicators provide useful warning without overwhelming the manager?
How should scenario accuracy be assessed when supplier promises change?
Does cited extraction improve review speed without hiding conflicting evidence?
new_work: Review extracted disruption signals and conflicting sources.
Resolve stale forecasts, identifier mismatches and missing delivery records.
Maintain scenario assumptions, thresholds and source permissions.
Monitor connectors and compare predicted shortages with actual outcomes.

tasks.short: Help define equipment, product and substitute-material specifications.

steps.what: Collect user requirements, existing specifications and supplier technical information.

loop.input: Purchase request, existing specifications and supplier technical sheets.
loop.output: Requirements pack with source-linked requirements, units and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate units and source references; flag contradictions and distinguish requirements from supplier claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; ambiguous requirements remain open for people.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technical requirements arrive in varied prose and document layouts.

steps.what: Agree essential performance, compatibility and commercial requirements with users and technical staff.
Compare options against requirements, costs and stated acceptance criteria.
Draft the specification and identify unresolved acceptance conditions.

loop.input: Agreed requirements, option comparison and approved specification template.
loop.output: Draft specification with traceable requirements and explicit unresolved conditions.
loop.check: Check required sections, units and requirement coverage; prohibit invented standards or acceptance thresholds.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing technical decisions return to the technical team.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirement wording and acceptance conditions vary by equipment and material.

steps.what: Review technical suitability and approve acceptance conditions using qualification evidence.
Publish the approved specification and attach it to the sourcing request.

tasks.design: A requirements record in {WORKFLOW} links source documents in {DOCS}, while deterministic checks compare units, costs and acceptance criteria. Bounded loops prepare requirements and specification drafts; technical approval releases the version into {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were spread across documents and conversations, with inconsistent templates and weak version control. Technical acceptance criteria could not safely be inferred from supplier claims.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, versioned templates and validation rules already handle much of the structure. AI-assisted coding makes a focused requirements app cheaper, and bounded drafting reduces repeated document assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Compatibility, safety and actual material performance need technical expertise and sometimes physical testing. Drafting cannot establish that a substitute will work.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve tradeoffs between user needs, technical performance, supplier capability and commercial practicality.

ambition.what: Source-linked substitute-material briefs for technical qualification

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time challenging unnecessary requirements and developing viable substitutes with technical staff. Technical acceptance and sourcing authority remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Turn specifications into comparable quotation requests.
reach.learn: Learn which specification ambiguities cause incomparable bids and supplier exclusions.

reach.task: Assess substitute products for an assortment.
reach.learn: Learn functional equivalence, customer expectations and margin implications.

evidence.claim: Structured requirement records, unit checks and version control can reduce specification administration.
Bounded extraction and drafting can prepare source-linked specifications, but technical qualification remains human.

assumptions: Procurement contributes commercial requirements; technical staff approve technical suitability.
Supplier documents and existing specifications are available in usable digital form.
Unlike the low model-needed prior, varied source documents justify two narrow loops; comparison remains deterministic.
Build ranges cover one specification family and exclude laboratory testing or engineering redesign.
EU GDPR applies to personal data in documents. Access and any required employee consultation under national rules are included.
unknowns: Which technical standards and qualification procedures apply to the customer's purchases.
Who can approve requirements, substitutions and specification releases.
Whether existing templates and requirement identifiers are consistent.
Whether supplier documents may be processed by the chosen model service.
research_questions: Which requirements can be checked mechanically without losing technical meaning?
How reliably can extraction distinguish mandatory requirements from descriptive supplier claims?
Which specification family offers a useful first implementation?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and draft wording.
Resolve conflicting units, missing acceptance criteria and unsupported supplier claims.
Maintain templates, approved terminology and validation rules.
Check source traceability and prevent superseded versions from being reused.

tasks.short: Keep order and receipt records complete, matched and current.

steps.what: Check approved orders and supplier delivery references.
Enter received quantities and delivery references from receiving evidence.
Match receipt lines to orders and identify missing or inconsistent entries.
Resolve receipt discrepancies with receiving staff and suppliers, approving supported corrections.
Copy order and receipt status into a shared tracking workbook.
File delivery evidence against the order and receipt records.

tasks.design: Configure receipt capture, matching rules and evidence attachments in {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, using their supported interfaces where records cross systems. Replace the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} tracker with a shared status view and route disputed corrections through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Receiving and procurement used different records, and a shared workbook filled visibility gaps. Missing references and inconsistent receipt practices prevented reliable matching.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing receipt screens, reference scanning and matching rules cover the routine work. AI-assisted coding can make small interface adaptations cheaper without introducing a model into record posting.
tasks.still_hard: Systems cannot establish what physically arrived without trustworthy receiving evidence. Partial deliveries, damaged goods and disputed quantities need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Establish the physical facts behind a discrepancy and decide which correction the evidence supports.
tasks.altitude: The manager reviews fewer routine record problems and can focus on recurring delivery failures. No new decision rights are created.

reach.task: Maintain order references and receipt evidence.
reach.learn: Learn receipt identifiers, correction trails and the evidence needed for invoice matching.
Learn how receipt exceptions distinguish supplier delays from internal recording failures.

evidence.claim: Order records, goods receipts, matching tolerances and document attachments are standard purchasing and finance functions.
Routine record matching needs deterministic rules; disputed physical receipts still require human evidence.

assumptions: The company already records orders and receipts in business systems; a workbook supplies a shared status view.
Receipt evidence is created by receiving staff, rather than inferred from supplier delivery notices.
The supplied high rule-coverage and low model-needed priors fit routine matching.
Exception work takes a meaningful share of the manager's involvement even when exceptions are rare across all receipts.
Configuration supports matching and attachments; custom integration is limited to gaps between systems.
EU GDPR applies to staff identifiers in logs. Individual productivity scoring is excluded; national consultation requirements are assessed before changing receipt capture.
unknowns: Whether the customer's systems support receipt matching, scanning and evidence attachments.
Which receipts currently lack reliable order or delivery references.
Who may correct quantities and which corrections require separate approval.
Whether the shared workbook contains information absent from the source systems.
Which retention periods, access roles and national consultation rules apply.
research_questions: Which validation rules catch material receipt errors without delaying routine postings?
Can shared system views replace every useful field in the duplicate tracker?
Which exception categories require physical inspection rather than record correction?
new_work: Handle unmatched receipts and disputed corrections.
Maintain reference mappings, tolerances and access permissions.
Monitor failed transfers and duplicate postings.
Audit correction trails and missing delivery evidence.

tasks.short: Negotiate supplier contracts and agree purchasing policies.

steps.what: Assemble spend, supplier performance, current terms and renewal dates.
Draft negotiation objectives, concession options and proposed supplier policy changes.

loop.input: Evidence pack, approved purchasing policy, calculated concession scenarios and manager instructions.
loop.output: Draft mandate with objectives, limits, policy departures and cited contract terms.
loop.check: Verify figures deterministically; cite existing clauses; the manager checks commercial logic and alternatives.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per mandate; missing limits or conflicting policies return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contract wording and commercial tradeoffs vary; a fixed template cannot explain all proposed departures.

steps.what: Approve concession limits and proposed departures from purchasing policy.
Negotiate commercial terms and supplier responsibilities within the approved mandate.
Prepare contract revisions and supplier policy wording from provisional terms.

loop.input: Provisional terms, current contract, approved clause library and purchasing policy.
loop.output: Tracked contract revisions and supplier policy wording with a change summary.
loop.check: Map each change to an agreed term; validate prices and dates; flag unapproved clauses and policy conflicts.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved legal language goes to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated terms must be expressed consistently across varied contract and policy language.

steps.what: Review contractual departures and approve legal wording.
Authorise signature and release the agreed contract and supplier policy.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles a negotiation pack from {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {CLM}, with deterministic concession calculations. Bounded loops draft mandates and contract changes in {DOCS}; configured approvals and {ESIGN} handle release while the manager conducts negotiations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spend evidence, supplier performance and clauses were scattered. Standard templates helped with paperwork but could not resolve commercial tradeoffs or safely authorise concessions.
tasks.enabler_now: Read-only integrations and deterministic calculations can prepare consistent evidence packs. AI-assisted coding reduces assembly effort, while bounded drafting can produce traceable revisions for review.
tasks.still_hard: Power imbalance, trust, supplier dependency and legal departures remain difficult. The manager must judge when to concede, escalate or walk away.
tasks.human_edge: Read the supplier's incentives, preserve the relationship and make credible concessions within an approved mandate.

ambition.what: Quarterly concession-package decisions for strategic supplier renewals

tasks.altitude: The manager has more preparation time for difficult supplier conversations and can revisit renewal options earlier. Signing authority and policy approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Negotiate repeat orders within approved contract terms.
reach.learn: Learn which concessions affect delivery reliability, total cost and future leverage.

reach.task: Maintain agreed terms and renewal records.
reach.learn: Learn how signed clauses become usable price tables, order conditions and renewal alerts.

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly, concession calculations, approval routing and signature administration can use deterministic technology.
Bounded drafting can support negotiation preparation without transferring concession or signing authority.
Reported Walmart and Pactum vendor figures show deals with 68% of equipment suppliers approached and 3% average savings in 2023.

assumptions: The company uses delegated commercial limits and an authorised signatory for binding contracts.
Negotiations produce provisional terms subject to the required contract approvals.
Legal counsel reviews departures rather than every routine order.
The digest negotiation case shows feasibility in a specific setting; it does not establish transferable results for this company.
The relationship-heavy prior supports keeping negotiation human while changing preparation and paperwork.
EU GDPR applies to contact information. Confidential contracts require controlled access; consultation under national rules is included where working practices change.
unknowns: Which spend data, contract records and supplier performance measures are accessible.
Which concession limits, signature powers and policy approval roles apply.
Whether approved clause libraries and reliable contract versions exist.
Whether supplier confidentiality terms permit model processing.
Which national rules and consultation arrangements affect rollout.
research_questions: Which concession calculations best reveal total cost and delivery tradeoffs?
Can reviewers trace every proposed clause change to an agreed commercial term?
Which contract families are sufficiently consistent for the first rollout?
new_work: Review draft mandates, clause changes and policy conflicts.
Maintain clause libraries, concession calculators and approval routing.
Resolve incomplete evidence and reconcile final terms with the approved mandate.
Monitor access, connector failures and unsigned or superseded contract versions.

role.altitude: The purchasing manager's week shifts from collecting evidence and maintaining documents toward supply decisions, technical tradeoffs and supplier negotiations. Routine processing falls, but commercial, technical and signing rights stay with existing accountable roles unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Purchasing agents: connect availability risks and approved specifications to usable sourcing options.
Wholesale and retail buyers: understand substitute demand, assortment effects and margins.
Procurement clerks: connect order, receipt and contract records into reliable evidence.
skills_to_grow: Requirement traceability and technical qualification literacy
Data quality, access control and exception design
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring supply-options service that combines availability scenarios, qualified substitute briefs and renewal concession packages. People approve technical acceptance, material tradeoffs and external commitments.
